experiences.title: Graduate Research Assistant
description: Conduct statistical and graph ML analysis on the Drosophila adult brain connectome (FlyWire FAFB v783, Hemibrain via Neuprint) using NetworkX, graspologic, scikit-learn, NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas; apply and compare modularity maximization (RenEEL), degree-corrected stochastic block models, and spectral embedding methods for neural community detection on subconnectomes spanning thousands of annotated synaptic connections.

Implement and compare spectral clustering pipelines — adjacency and Laplacian spectral embedding (ASE/LSE) with Gaussian mixture models, grounded in the ASE central limit theorem (Priebe et al. 2017) — demonstrating that ASE-derived communities are spatially compartmentalized along dendritic anatomy and recover non-assortative feedforward motifs invisible to modularity-based methods by construction.

Designed and implemented a consensus clustering pipeline (100-run co-assignment matrices with hierarchical clustering, following Lancichinetti & Fortunato 2012) to address stochasticity in mixture-model partitions prior to biological interpretation, ensuring cluster assignments are robust rather than artifacts of a single run.

Co-authored abstract published in CSHL Neuronal Circuits 2026 Abstract Book (p. 68); abstract accepted for presentation at Cognitive Computational Neuroscience (CCN) 2026 (to appear in conference proceedings); co-authoring peer-reviewed manuscript on network-level synapse localization for journal submission under PI Dr. Gabrielle Gutierrez at Barnard's Neural Computation Lab.

Consolidated fragmented research scripts into reusable, dataset-agnostic Python modules (e.g. gmm_ase_pipeline.py, consensus_pipeline.py) with a shared fetch-function interface, parity checks between notebook and script logic, and full inline documentation — reducing redundant reimplementation and ensuring reproducibility across contributors and datasets.

Apply multivariate statistical methods and graph-theoretic measures (modularity, Q-value comparison across datasets, block-level spatial synapse distribution) to characterize mesoscale structure in biological neural networks, bridging spectral graph theory with neuroscience questions about how network organization reflects anatomical and functional compartmentalization.
